depth_findings.text: stream_call_usage prices each call with state.pricing.priced(), which runs ensure_fresh() per call; with a cold or unreachable cost-core every provider call while the flag is on can wait on a catalogue fetch up to FETCH_TIMEOUT, where the turn-end snapshot did it once. Fix before the flag goes on: take one pricing.snapshot() per turn and price from it.

Each usage.progress projection goes through onUiEvent, which use-chat-controller appends to uiEvents, and the trace and work feed render every event and count them; once the flag is on, each provider call adds a trace row, so S4 must filter progress out of the trace before the flag is switched on.

No handler-level test proves that the last usage_progress frame equals the terminal usage totals and precedes it; coverage is one source-order guard plus the sink unit tests, so the live SSE transcript with the flag on is still owed.

The answer's progress frame states the end-of-turn total priced from one RateSnapshot while tool-round frames are priced per call, so a catalogue refresh mid-turn can make the last progress total differ from the usage frame; the usage frame stays the authority by design, and the live run should measure the gap.
No test shows that a switched-off sink never reads the catalogue (stream_call_usage returns before pricing); add a counting wiremock on /api/v1/pricing to lock that in.

Judge and resample verification calls (judge_sources and resample_answer in sse.rs) also stream usage_progress frames because the row asks for one per provider call; the owner should confirm progress frames for verification calls are wanted.
The fallback answer path (run_infer_fallback) reads the switch itself rather than from the sink, so one turn has two readers of the same switch; pass the sink's flag or one value per turn.
Progress frames ride the sink's resume buffer under the existing sync_cursor stretches, and no test covers a reconnect during the tool phase replaying them in order.

The SPA native usage_progress case reads Record<string, unknown> because the generated payload types lack the key until the golden is regenerated; switch it to ChatEventPayloads['usage_progress'] then, as the usage case does.
The progress payload carries no request_id (the closed key list), so a consumer correlates by stream only; confirm that is enough for S4's meter.

tool_loop::stream_call_usage calls state.pricing.priced() once per provider call (ensure_fresh each time), so with the switch on and cost-core cold or unreachable, each call can wait up to the catalogue fetch timeout. Price from one per-turn snapshot before the switch goes on.

The SPA now projects usage.progress through PROJECTABLE_CUSTOM_NAMES and onUiEvent, so each provider call will add a trace or work-feed row once the switch is on. S4 must filter progress events out of the trace before the flip.

Only a source-order guard (the_answer_progress_frame_precedes_the_usage_frame_with_the_turn_total) proves that the last progress frame precedes and equals the terminal usage frame. No handler-level stream test checks it, so the live SSE transcript is still owed.

Tool-round and overhead frames are priced per call against the live catalogue, while the answer frame states turn_usage's single-snapshot total. A catalogue refresh mid-turn can therefore make cost_usd non-monotonic or jump at the answer frame.

run_infer_fallback reads usage_progress_switch() itself instead of the sink's flag, so one turn reads the switch twice. Toggling the env mid-turn can give tool-round frames without an answer frame, or the reverse.
No test proves that a switched-off sink never reads the pricing catalogue (the early return in stream_call_usage). A counting mock on /api/v1/pricing would lock that in.
No test covers reconnect or resume replay of progress frames buffered through the sink's resume buffer during the tool phase.

depth_findings.text: Under zero retention a workspace AI run gets a bare 401 instead of the typed feature_not_supported browser_run refusal: model-gateway browser_run_start extracts VerifiedBrowserBearer before its ZDR check, the BFF sends no browser bearer under ZDR, and the BFF then reports the 401 as 'Quarry browser session is not available'. Fix before the switch goes on, by refusing ZDR before the bearer extractor in browser_run.rs or by refusing in the BFF.

Owner to confirm the host policy for a run that names no hosts: the only SPA caller (KnowledgeComposer.tsx startBrowserAiRun) sends goal and maxSteps only, so the BFF grants the current page host alone, and an explicit host list that omits that page fails at derive with 'start_url is outside the broker grant policy'.

The org site policy narrows a grant only when the broker runs with BROWSER_BROKER_SITE_POLICY shadow or enforce. The default is off (ParseMode of empty is off, go/services/browser-broker/internal/sitepolicy/client.go) and the Model Plane deploy compose sets no value, so the BFF switch must not go on before the broker mode is set, in the S10 order.

Before the switch goes on, Quarry (quarryv2, not on model-plane) must accept the broker-issued session and derived run grant ids on its run path, and the lead must prove a workspace AI run on a rebuilt stack with browser-workspace-hitl.spec.ts and browser-workspace-session.spec.ts. Neither was run here.

A run that fails after its session grant is issued leaves that grant live until the broker TTL, because the BFF never calls model-gateway DELETE /v1/browser/grants/:grant_id (browser_grants.rs) when a run start fails. Model-gateway already revokes its own derived run grants on failure.

The plan says the workspace run forwards the bearer 'through browser_token', but that gate needs BROWSER_DO_ENABLED and an agentic chat body, so this slice mints aud=browser-broker through require_model_service_token under BROWSER_AI_RUN_REAL_GRANT alone. Owner to confirm that no second switch is wanted.

Workspace runs carry no Space scope and WS21-S8's browser_entitled floor does not gate them. That is safe only while browser sessions are never Space-scoped, which browser.rs does not do today; keep it that way or add the floor before any Space-scoped browser session exists.

Every workspace run creates a new broker session grant (session_key ui-<ulid>), so repeated runs can reach the per-parent cap and return too_many_browser_grants (429) until TTLs release them. Measure before default-on.

proxy_model_json_with_browser repeats the header set of chat/shared.rs proxy_model_json_with_delegations, because the shared helper has no browser slot and shared.rs is not in this slice. Fold the slot into the shared helper when that file is next edited.

forward_quarry_failure answers any model-gateway failure without an error key with 'Quarry browser session is not available', which misreports the grant and run routes now that they are model-gateway calls. A model-gateway-specific message would fix it.
No test reaches a typed zero-retention refusal from the workspace run. Add one together with the fix for depth finding 1.
The error branches of issue_ai_run_grant are untested: a 201 with no grant_id (502 browser_grant_invalid) and an unreadable allowed_domains list (502).

Plan and extraction drift: WS21.json says the model-gateway POST /v1/browser/grants route and the broker sitepolicy package are absent, but both exist (browser_grants.rs wired at http_routes.rs:320; broker commit 76e1b9fd3). The S7 row should name browser_grants.rs as the issuance route.

When the switch is on, a zero-retention workspace run still sends the session:{id} string and no browser bearer, so model-gateway browser_run_start returns a bare 401 from its VerifiedBrowserBearer extractor, not a typed feature_not_supported refusal. forward_quarry_failure then shows that 401 as 'Quarry browser session is not available'. Fix this in browser_run.rs or in the BFF before the switch goes on.

The org site policy narrows the issued grant only when the broker runs with BROWSER_BROKER_SITE_POLICY set to shadow or enforce, and that defaults to off. BROWSER_AI_RUN_REAL_GRANT must not go on before the broker mode is set.

Owner to confirm the host default. If the request names no hosts, the grant covers only the current page host. If the request names hosts that leave out the current page, model-gateway refuses the run at derive with start_url outside the grant policy.

If a run fails to start after issue_ai_run_grant succeeded, the session grant stays live until the broker TTL. The BFF never calls DELETE /v1/browser/grants/:grant_id, and each run creates a new ui-<ulid> session grant, so repeated failures can reach too_many_browser_grants.

The bearer is minted through require_model_service_token(BrowserBroker) under BROWSER_AI_RUN_REAL_GRANT alone, not through browser_token as the plan row says. The deviation is reasoned, because the browser_token gate cannot hold for a workspace run, but the owner should confirm.

proxy_model_json_with_browser copies proxy_model_json_with_delegations from chat/shared.rs, with the same headers when no browser bearer is passed. Fold a browser slot into the shared helper the next time shared.rs is in scope.
